case_name: Board Of School Education v Arun Rathi
respondent:
Arun Rathi
Supreme Court of India

9 February 1994
Civil Appeal Nos. 690-93 of 1994
The Judgment was delivered by : S. C. Agrawal, J.
Special leave granted.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
1. These appeals raise the question whether a candidate who has taken the Senior Secondary Certificate Examination of the Board of School Education, Haryana (hereinafter referred to as 'the Board') is entitled to the award of grace marks so as to enable him to earn compartment. The respondents in these appeals appeared in the Senior Secondary Certificate Examination of the Board held in the month of March 1993 but were declared as failed since they did not secure the minimum pass marks in two of the subjects. They moved the High Court of Punjab & Haryana, by filing writ petitions under Article 226 of the Constitution and claimed that they should be awarded grace marks and be placed under compartment, so as to enable them to appear in the supplementary examination in
facts: The respondents in these appeals appeared in the Senior Secondary Certificate Examination of the Board held in the month of March 1993 but were declared as failed since they did not secure the minimum pass marks in two of the subjects.

In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 19(1) of the Act the Board has made the Haryana Senior Secondary Certificate Examination Regulations, 1990 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Regulations')
The said writ petitions have been allowed by the High Court by orders dated September 6, 1993 and September 10, 1993.

Following the said decision a Division Bench of the High Court in Anil Kumar v. Board of School Education, Haryana, Civil Misc. No.6963 of 1990 and Writ Petition (Civil) No.9164 of 1990, decided on Aug.18, 1990 (P & H, DB) directed the Board to award grace marks so as to entitle the petitioner in that case to earn a compartment.
It was also decided that a proposal to carry out amendment in the relevant Regulations be considered in the next meeting of the Board.

The question whether the concession of grace marks could be given to students for earning compartment came up for consideration before a Full Bench of the High Court in Raj Kumar v. State Board of Technical Education, Punjab, (1990) 2 Punj LR 179 1990 Indlaw PNH 96, 185

Recently another Full Bench of the High Court in Anita Devi v. State of Haryana, (1993) 2 Punj LR 157 1993 Indlaw PNH 228 has considered the question of confining the award of grace marks only to a candidate who can pass the examination but not if he is placed in compartment
The validity of the said provision was assailed as being violative of Article 14 of the Constitution and reliance was placed on the decision in Naresh Shosi case (supra).
issues: Whether a candidate who has taken the Senior Secondary Certificate Examination of the Board of School Education, Haryana is entitled to the award of grace marks so as to enable him to earn compartment

Whether Regulation 26(b) of the Regulations, insofar as it debars a failed candidate to the entitlement of the benefit of grace marks in order to earn compartment is arbitrary and violative of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution
Whether the concession of grace marks could be given to students for earning compartment
Whether Regulation 26 came up for consideration before a Full Bench of the High Court, Punjab & Haryana in Meenakshi Sharma v. Board of School Education, Haryana
petitioner_arguments: The respondents in these appeals argued that they should be awarded grace marks and be placed under compartment, so as to enable them to appear in the supplementary examination in one paper in September 1993

It was observed that if the regulation was capable of the interpretation that grace marks could not be awarded to a candidate if by awarding such marks he can earn compartment then the regulation would be held to be arbitrary and discriminatory

The Court rejected the contention urged on behalf of the Board that the decision in Naresh Shosi case (supra) was not applicable in view of the express provision regarding non-award of grace marks in the Regulations of the Board

It has been observed 'The academic standards laid down by the appropriate authorities postulate the minimum marks that a candidate has to secure before he becomes eligible for the award of the diploma'
Normally, the Court shall be slow to extend the concession of grace marks and grant a benefit where none is intended to be given by the appropriate authority
respondent_arguments: The Board argued that Regulation 26(b) of the Regulations, insofar as it debars a failed candidate to the entitlement of the benefit of grace marks in order to earn compartment is not arbitrary and violative of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution
The Board also proposed an amendment in Regulation 26 in the light of the decision of the High Court in Anil Kumar case, (supra) and the same was forwarded to the State Government for approval
It has been observed 'The award of grace marks is a concession. It results in diluting academic standards'

Rejecting the contention that the absence of a provision regarding concession of grace marks for earning compartment though a provision is made about the grant of grace marks for passing out the examinations, renders the rule discriminatory, the Full Bench has observed
court_reasoning: The Court rejected the contention urged on behalf of the Board that the decision in Naresh Shosi case (supra) was not applicable in view of the express provision regarding non-award of grace marks in the Regulations of the Board

It was observed that if the regulation was capable of the interpretation that grace marks could not be awarded to a candidate if by awarding such marks he can earn compartment then the regulation would be held to be arbitrary and discriminatory
The Court has agreed with the earlier Full Bench decision in Raj Kumar case1990 Indlaw PNH 96 (supra)

It has been observed 'The academic standards laid down by the appropriate authorities postulate the minimum marks that a candidate has to secure before he becomes eligible for the award of the diploma'
Normally, the Court shall be slow to extend the concession of grace marks and grant a benefit where none is intended to be given by the appropriate authority
holding: The Supreme Court granted special leave and allowed the appeals

The Court held that Regulation 26(b) of the Regulations, insofar as it debars a failed candidate to the entitlement of the benefit of grace marks in order to earn compartment is arbitrary and violative of Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution
The Court also held that the concession of grace marks could be given to students for earning compartment
